agent.name: Emerging Technology Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Contextual adoption decision for Waymo robotaxis

analytical_question: Should DesertLink put Waymo-operated Phoenix rides on its platform now?
general_et_finding: Waymo robotaxis are operating commercially in Phoenix and have substantial rider-only mileage, although deployment is bounded and safety risk persists.
application_finding: Existing Phoenix service suggests a strong fit for on-demand passenger trips in Waymo's area.
organization_specific_finding: DesertLink is a moderate fast follower with an existing booking operation, so it can test the service rather than replace its human-driver fleet.

evidence.claim: Waymo offers driverless rides in Metro Phoenix.
Waymo reports 271.3 million rider-only miles through June 2026 across listed cities.
A 2026 recall report identifies a freeway-construction-zone risk.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Commercial integration access and economics for DesertLink have not been verified.
The NHTSA recall shows that operational boundaries and software controls matter.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in general deployment; low confidence in DesertLink-specific feasibility because agreement, permissions and unit economics are unknown.
value_opportunity_implication: A partner ride option could increase availability and perhaps shorten waits, but this is unmeasured for DesertLink.
risk_governance_implication: Keep trips inside the service domain and arrange incident escalation with Waymo.
recommendation_management_implication: Conduct a bounded passenger pilot now: offer up to 100 Waymo rides through DesertLink over one month, then decide whether to scale.
change_monitoring_triggers: Pilot rider wait times and incident rate
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Obtain a commercial agreement, permit allocation, insurance and pricing details before a large launch.
